newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya calls for end to foreign role in Zaire war.
newsitem.headline: Kenya calls for end to foreign role in Zaire war.

text.p: Kenya's President Daniel arap Moi on Friday urged countries involved in the war in Zaire to stop and called on rebels to observe an immediate ceasefire.
Moi said continuing the conflict would lead to the destabilisation of Zaire and the entire Great Lakes region.

"President Daniel arap Moi called on all those countries fuelling the conflict in Zaire by being directly involved or by supplying weapons to stop at once," the presidential press service quoted a statement from State House in Nairobi saying.

"Noting that their resort to armed conflict had greatly complicated the situation, President Moi called upon the Banyamulenge to immediately observe a ceasefire and withdraw so as to assist in advancing the cause of peace," it added.
"Such an act will encourage the international community to galvanise all efforts in the search for lasting peace and stability in the entire Great Lakes region," the president added.
Moi is the chairman of a group of African heads of state charged with helping end conflict in the Great Lakes region and called for the respect of the territorial integrity of Zaire.
Calls by two summits of African leaders for an immediate ceasefire in Zaire have been ignored and Kinshasa has rejected negotiations with the rebels, who launched their revolt in October.
The presidential press service said Moi noted reports that foreign countries were supporting Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels in their fight against Zaire. But he did not name them.
"Moi said Kenya wished to underscore the fact that Banyamulenge are Zaire citizens and urged them to address their grievances against the government by peaceful means," it added.
The Banyamulenge said they rebelled because they were denied citizenship and were threatened with expulsion by authorities. Their rebel alliance has seized a swathe of territory in the east.
Zaire's defence ministry on Thursday expressed "satisfaction" at a U.S. call for Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi to respect Kinshasa's territorial integrity and stay out of the fighting.
The United States did not directly accuse Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of intervening in neighbouring eastern Zaire but U.S. officials in Washington said there had been allegations of this.
Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi have repeatedly denied Zairean charges that they had sent their troops into eastern Zaire to fight alongside the rebel alliance against government forces.
The European Commission said on Thursday it had invited Moi and President Yoweri Museveni for talks on the war in Zaire.
The two do not see eye-to-eye on the situation in the Great Lakes region and have also been at odds on other matters such as Rwanda, when Uganda backed Tutsi rebels who took power in 1994.
